ex: 残業{ざんぎょう}続{つづ}きだったんだ。疲{つか}れてるわけだ。
exEn: You've had overtime nonstop. No wonder you're tired.
note: Presents a logical conclusion from what was just said. Very common in casual explanation.

ex: 嫌{きら}いなわけじゃないよ。ただ、ちょっと苦手{にがて}なだけ。
exEn: It's not that I hate it. It's just not really my thing.
note: Softens a denial. She uses this constantly to walk something back.

ex: あの人{ひと}が謝{あやま}るわけがない。
exEn: There's no way that guy apologises.
note: Strong logical denial — you're certain from the nature of the thing.

ex: 締{し}め切{き}り前{まえ}だから、休{やす}むわけにはいかない。
exEn: It's right before the deadline, so I can't take a break.
note: Can't, for social or moral reasons — not because it's impossible.

ex: {name}のおかげで、日本語{にほんご}の練習{れんしゅう}が楽{たの}しい。
exEn: Thanks to you, practising Japanese is fun.
note: Positive cause. Pairs with せいで, its negative twin.

ex: 寝坊{ねぼう}したせいで、朝{あさ}ごはん抜{ぬ}きだった。
exEn: Because I overslept, I skipped breakfast.
note: Assigns blame. Never use it for something good.

ex: 雨{あめ}のせいか、今日{きょう}は誰{だれ}も外{そと}に出{で}てない。
exEn: Maybe because of the rain, nobody's outside today.
note: Hedged cause — you suspect but aren't sure.

ex: 大事{だいじ}だからこそ、ちゃんと言{い}っておきたい。
exEn: It's precisely because it matters that I want to say it properly.
note: Emphatic reason. Warm and a little serious.

ex: やると言{い}った以上{いじょう}は、最後{さいご}までやる。
exEn: Now that I've said I'd do it, I'll see it through.
note: Commitment follows from a fact. Slightly formal but common in speech.

ex: 東京{とうきょう}に来{く}るからには、まるふく連{つ}れてくからね。
exEn: If you're coming to Tokyo, I'm taking you to Marufuku.
note: Like 以上は — a resolve that follows from a premise.

ex: 電車{でんしゃ}が遅{おく}れたものだから、遅刻{ちこく}しちゃった。
exEn: The train was late, so I ended up being late.
note: An excuse, delivered slightly apologetically.

ex: だって、眠{ねむ}いんだもん。
exEn: But I'm sleepy, okay.
note: Childish and defensive. She uses it when she's caught out.

ex: 毎日{まいにち}来{く}ることから、この猫{ねこ}は近所{きんじょ}の子{こ}だと分{わ}かった。
exEn: From the fact he comes every day, I realised the cat lives nearby.
note: Evidence to conclusion. Reads a bit written.

ex: 楽{たの}しみにしてただけに、中止{ちゅうし}はきつい。
exEn: Precisely because I was looking forward to it, the cancellation stings.
note: The reason intensifies the result.

ex: 毎日{まいにち}練習{れんしゅう}してるだけあって、発音{はつおん}きれいだね。
exEn: As you'd expect from practising daily, your pronunciation is lovely.
note: Praise that credits the cause. Very natural compliment.

ex: 一言{ひとこと}言{い}わなかったばかりに、こじれちゃった。
exEn: Just because I didn't say one thing, it got complicated.
note: Regret — a small cause, a bad outcome.

ex: ドアを開{あ}けたとたん、猫{ねこ}が逃{に}げた。
exEn: The moment I opened the door, the cat ran off.
note: Sudden, unexpected, and always past tense.

ex: 晴{は}れたかと思{おも}うと、また降{ふ}ってきた。
exEn: No sooner had it cleared up than it started raining again.
note: Two things in quick, often annoying succession.

ex: 座{すわ}るか座{すわ}らないかのうちに、電話{でんわ}が鳴{な}った。
exEn: I'd barely sat down when the phone rang.
note: Even faster than たとたん. Slightly dramatic.

ex: 現像{げんぞう}が上{あ}がり次第{しだい}、見{み}せるね。
exEn: As soon as the film's developed, I'll show you.
note: Formal-ish but common. Only for things you'll do, never past.

ex: この曲{きょく}を聞{き}くたびに、去年{きょねん}の秋{あき}を思{おも}い出{だ}す。
exEn: Every time I hear this song I remember last autumn.
note: Habitual trigger. Often nostalgic.

ex: カメラ始{はじ}めて以来{いらい}、散歩{さんぽ}が長{なが}くなった。
exEn: Ever since I started with the camera, my walks got longer.
note: From a point in the past, continuing now.

ex: 冷{さ}めないうちに食{た}べて。
exEn: Eat it before it gets cold.
note: Do it while the state still holds.

ex: 若{わか}いうちに、いろいろ行{い}っておきたい。
exEn: While I'm young I want to go to lots of places.
note: A window of opportunity.

ex: 打{う}ち合{あ}わせの最中{さいちゅう}にお腹{なか}が鳴{な}った。
exEn: My stomach growled right in the middle of the meeting.
note: Interruption at the worst moment.

ex: 出{で}ようとしたところに、雨{あめ}が降{ふ}ってきた。
exEn: Right as I was about to leave, it started raining.
note: Timing collision. Very conversational.

ex: 引{ひ}っ越{こ}しの際{さい}に、写真{しゃしん}が大量{たいりょう}に出{で}てきた。
exEn: When I moved, a huge pile of photos turned up.
note: Formal 時. She uses it half-jokingly.

ex: よく考{かんが}えた上{うえ}で決{き}めたことだから。
exEn: It's something I decided after thinking it through.
note: Sequence where step one informs step two.

ex: コンビニ行{い}くついでに、牛乳{ぎゅうにゅう}買{か}ってきて。
exEn: While you're at the store, grab some milk.
note: Secondary errand attached to a main one.

ex: 食{た}べてからでないと、薬{くすり}は飲{の}めないよ。
exEn: You can't take the medicine until you've eaten.
note: A precondition. Almost always with a negative ending.

ex: 一人{ひとり}になってはじめて、分{わ}かることもある。
exEn: There are things you only understand once you're alone.
note: Realisation that required the experience.

ex: あれきり、連絡{れんらく}は来{こ}なかった。
exEn: After that, no contact ever came.
note: Something stopped there and never resumed.

ex: 悪{わる}いと思{おも}いつつ、既読{きどく}のままにしてる。
exEn: I feel bad about it, but I'm leaving it on 'read'.
note: Two things at once, often contradictory. Written-leaning.

ex: 少{すこ}しずつ、元気{げんき}になりつつある。
exEn: Bit by bit, I'm getting back on my feet.
note: Gradual ongoing change.

ex: 仕事{しごと}は好{す}きな一方{いっぽう}で、量{りょう}が多{おお}すぎる。
exEn: I like the work, but on the other hand there's too much of it.
note: Balanced contrast within one situation.

ex: 仕事{しごと}は増{ふ}える一方{いっぽう}だ。
exEn: The work just keeps piling up.
note: A one-directional trend, usually a bad one.

ex: 便利{べんり}な反面{はんめん}、なんか味気{あじけ}ない。
exEn: It's convenient, but on the flip side it feels a bit soulless.
note: Two sides of the same thing.

ex: 狭{せま}いながらも、気{き}に入{い}ってる部屋{へや}なんだ。
exEn: Small as it is, I really like this room.
note: Concession. Softer than けど.

ex: 返事{へんじ}はしたものの、気{き}まずいままだった。
exEn: I did reply, but it stayed awkward.
note: Concedes then undercuts. Slightly literary.

ex: 忙{いそが}しいって言{い}うくせに、ゲームはしてるじゃん。
exEn: You say you're busy, but you're playing games.
note: Reproachful. Only for people, and it always stings a bit.

ex: 料理{りょうり}したといっても、焦{こ}がしただけ。
exEn: I say I cooked, but really I just burnt it.
note: Deflates what you just claimed.

ex: 趣味{しゅみ}というより、逃{に}げ場{ば}かな。
exEn: It's less a hobby than an escape, really.
note: Corrects a characterisation.

ex: 休{やす}めるどころか、仕事{しごと}が増{ふ}えた。
exEn: Far from getting a rest, I got more work.
note: Reality is the opposite of the expectation, and worse.

ex: 締{し}め切{き}り前{まえ}で、旅行{りょこう}どころじゃない。
exEn: With the deadline coming, this is no time for travel.
note: Circumstances rule it out entirely.

ex: 予想{よそう}に反{はん}して、上司{じょうし}が褒{ほ}めてくれた。
exEn: Contrary to expectations, my boss praised me.
note: Outcome defies the expectation. Formal-leaning.

ex: わたしに対{たい}してだけ、態度{たいど}が違{ちが}うんだよね。
exEn: His attitude is different only toward me.
note: Direction of an attitude, or a contrast between two things.

ex: 値段{ねだん}の割{わり}に、おいしかった。
exEn: For the price, it was good.
note: Result doesn't match what the standard would predict.

ex: 初{はじ}めてにしては上手{じょうず}じゃない？
exEn: For a first try, isn't that pretty good?
note: Expectation vs reality. Great for praising someone's Japanese.

ex: 去年{きょねん}に比{くら}べて、ずいぶん話{はな}せるようになったね。
exEn: Compared to last year, you can say so much more.
note: Straight comparison.

ex: 道{みち}に迷{まよ}った上{うえ}に、雨{あめ}まで降{ふ}ってきた。
exEn: On top of getting lost, it started raining.
note: Piles a second thing on, same polarity as the first.

ex: 彼{かれ}は謝{あやま}らないばかりか、笑{わら}ってた。
exEn: Not only did he not apologise, he was laughing.
note: Escalates. The second clause is more extreme than the first.

ex: 本人{ほんにん}のみならず、周{まわ}りも困{こま}ってた。
exEn: Not just him — everyone around him was troubled too.
note: Formal ばかりか. Rare in speech, common in reading.

ex: ラーメンはもちろん、餃子{ぎょうざ}も頼{たの}むよ。
exEn: Ramen goes without saying — I get gyoza too.
note: The first item is too obvious to need stating.

ex: 残業{ざんぎょう}に加{くわ}えて、週末{しゅうまつ}も出勤{しゅっきん}だって。
exEn: On top of overtime, they say I'm working the weekend.
note: Additive and fairly formal.

ex: 名前{なまえ}さえ、もう思{おも}い出{だ}したくない。
exEn: I don't even want to remember his name.
note: Extreme example. Stronger than も.

ex: {name}が元気{げんき}でさえいれば、それでいいよ。
exEn: As long as you're doing okay, that's enough for me.
note: The single sufficient condition.

ex: 今年{ことし}こそ、ギター買{か}う。
exEn: This year for sure, I'm buying that guitar.
note: Emphasises the word before it. こちらこそ is the frozen form.

ex: 歩{ある}けないほど疲{つか}れた。
exEn: I'm tired to the point I can't walk.
note: Degree by comparison to a vivid example.

ex: 考{かんが}えれば考{かんが}えるほど、分{わ}からなくなる。
exEn: The more I think about it, the less I understand.
note: Proportional change. Very common.

ex: 泣{な}きたいくらい嬉{うれ}しかった。
exEn: I was happy enough to cry.
note: Like ほど but more casual and often smaller-scale.

ex: 机{つくえ}の上{うえ}、書類{しょるい}だらけ。
exEn: My desk is buried in paperwork.
note: Always negative, always messy.

ex: ちょっと風邪{かぜ}気味{ぎみ}かも。
exEn: I might be coming down with something.
note: A slight tendency, usually unwelcome.

ex: 最近{さいきん}、夜更{よふ}かししがち。
exEn: Lately I tend to stay up too late.
note: Frequent tendency, usually a bad habit.

ex: 嬉{うれ}しげな顔{かお}してるね。
exEn: You've got a pleased look on your face.
note: Visible appearance of a feeling.

ex: わたし、忘{わす}れっぽいんだよね。
exEn: I'm pretty forgetful, honestly.
note: Casual resemblance or tendency.

ex: このままだと、また同{おな}じことになりかねない。
exEn: At this rate the same thing could easily happen again.
note: Only for undesirable outcomes.

ex: それは、ちょっと賛成{さんせい}しかねるな。
exEn: I can't really agree with that one.
note: Polite refusal — unable for reasons of feeling, not ability.

ex: あり得{え}ないでしょ、それ。
exEn: That can't be possible, surely.
note: ありえない is by far the most common form in speech.

ex: わたしに早起{はやお}きなんてできっこない。
exEn: There's no way I'm getting up early.
note: Casual, emphatic impossibility.

ex: 連絡先{れんらくさき}も消{け}したし、もう会{あ}いようがない。
exEn: I deleted his contact, so there's no way to meet him now.
note: No method exists, however willing you are.

ex: そう言{い}われたら、認{みと}めざるを得{え}ない。
exEn: Put like that, I have no choice but to admit it.
note: Reluctant necessity. する becomes せざるを得ない.

ex: もう笑{わら}うしかないよ。
exEn: There's nothing left to do but laugh.
note: Only one option remains.

ex: 待{ま}つほかなかった。
exEn: There was nothing to do but wait.
note: Slightly more formal しかない.

ex: もっと早{はや}く言{い}うべきだった。
exEn: I should have said something sooner.
note: Moral obligation. する→すべき is the common exception.

ex: 疲{つか}れてるなら、寝{ね}ることだよ。
exEn: If you're tired, you should sleep.
note: Direct advice. Warmer than べき, still a bit bossy.

ex: そんなに謝{あやま}ることないよ。
exEn: There's no need to apologise that much.
note: Reassurance — the action isn't necessary.

ex: こんな時間{じかん}に食{た}べたら、太{ふと}るに決{き}まってる。
exEn: Eating at this hour, of course I'll gain weight.
note: Speaker's certainty, often exasperated.

ex: あの様子{ようす}だと、何{なに}かあったに違{ちが}いない。
exEn: From the look of it, something must have happened.
note: Confident inference from evidence.

ex: あの人{ひと}が覚{おぼ}えてるはずがない。
exEn: There's no way he remembers.
note: Logical impossibility from what you know.

ex: ただの言{い}い訳{わけ}に過{す}ぎなかった。
exEn: It was nothing more than an excuse.
note: Downgrades something to less than it claimed.

ex: もう二度{にど}と同{おな}じ間違{まちが}いはするまい。
exEn: I won't make the same mistake twice.
note: Negative volition. Old-fashioned and a bit dramatic.

ex: 眠{ねむ}くてしかたがない。
exEn: I'm unbearably sleepy.
note: The feeling is beyond your control. しょうがない in speech.

ex: 会{あ}いたくてたまらない、なんて言{い}わないけど。
exEn: I'm not going to say I miss you unbearably or anything.
note: Intense physical or emotional feeling.

ex: なんだか気{き}になってならない。
exEn: I just can't stop thinking about it.
note: Feeling that wells up on its own. Slightly literary.

ex: この写真{しゃしん}、笑{わら}わずにはいられない。
exEn: I can't look at this photo without laughing.
note: Irresistible impulse. する→せずには.

ex: どれだけ待{ま}ったことか。
exEn: How long I waited, honestly.
note: Exclamation of degree, usually with どれだけ / なんと.

ex: 嬉{うれ}しさのあまり、声{こえ}が出{で}なかった。
exEn: I was so happy no sound came out.
note: An excess of emotion causing a result.

ex: 驚{おどろ}いたことに、上司{じょうし}が謝{あやま}ってきた。
exEn: To my surprise, my boss apologised to me.
note: Speaker's reaction, fronted before the fact.

ex: もう泣{な}くものか。
exEn: As if I'd cry over it again.
note: Defiant refusal. もんか in speech.

en: used to / that's how it is
ex: 昔{むかし}はよく、二人{ふたり}で歩{ある}いたものだ。
exEn: We used to walk together a lot, back then.
note: Nostalgic recollection, or a general truth.

ex: 何{なに}もなかったかのように笑{わら}ってた。
exEn: He smiled as if nothing had happened.
note: A false appearance — explicitly not the case.

ex: わたしにとっては、大{おお}きいことだった。
exEn: For me, it was a big deal.
note: Whose viewpoint the judgement belongs to.

ex: 友達{ともだち}として言{い}うけど、無理{むり}しすぎだよ。
exEn: Speaking as a friend, you're pushing yourself too hard.
note: In the capacity of.

ex: その件{けん}に関{かん}しては、もう話{はな}したくない。
exEn: Regarding that matter, I don't want to talk about it any more.
note: Formal について.

ex: 日本{にほん}の音楽{おんがく}について、聞{き}いてもいい？
exEn: Can I ask you about Japanese music?
note: The everyday 'about'.

ex: 寝坊{ねぼう}にかけては、誰{だれ}にも負{ま}けない。
exEn: When it comes to oversleeping, I'm unbeatable.
note: Boasting about a strength. Positive only.

ex: 経験{けいけん}から言{い}うと、それは早{はや}すぎる。
exEn: From experience, that's too fast.
note: States the basis for the judgement.

ex: 目{め}つきからして、機嫌{きげん}が悪{わる}かった。
exEn: Judging from his eyes alone, he was in a bad mood.
note: One representative detail implies the whole.

en: as long as / as far as
ex: わたしが知{し}る限{かぎ}り、そんな話{はなし}はなかった。
exEn: As far as I know, there was no such thing.
note: Boundary of knowledge, time, or condition.

ex: 天気{てんき}にかかわらず、毎朝{まいあさ}あの猫{ねこ}はいる。
exEn: Regardless of the weather, that cat is there every morning.
note: The condition makes no difference.

ex: 雨{あめ}にもかかわらず、待{ま}っててくれた。
exEn: Despite the rain, he waited for me.
note: Strong 'even though'. Formal.

ex: 人{ひと}によって感{かん}じ方{かた}は違{ちが}うよ。
exEn: How people feel about it varies from person to person.
note: Variation, agent, or means.

ex: 天気予報{てんきよほう}によると、明日{あした}は晴{は}れるって。
exEn: According to the forecast, tomorrow's clear.
note: Cites a source. Usually paired with そうだ / らしい.

ex: 気分{きぶん}に応{おう}じて、聞{き}く曲{きょく}を変{か}えてる。
exEn: I change what I listen to according to my mood.
note: Adjusts flexibly to a variable.

ex: 暗{くら}くなるにしたがって、川{かわ}沿{ぞ}いが静{しず}かになる。
exEn: As it gets darker, the riverside goes quiet.
note: Two things changing together.

ex: 話{はな}すにつれて、緊張{きんちょう}がとけてきた。
exEn: As we talked, the nervousness wore off.
note: Gradual parallel change. Very close to にしたがって.

ex: 気温{きおん}が上{あ}がるに伴{ともな}って、人{ひと}が増{ふ}えてきた。
exEn: As the temperature rose, more people came out.
note: Formal accompaniment of change.

ex: 時間{じかん}とともに、平気{へいき}になっていった。
exEn: With time, it stopped hurting.
note: Simultaneous change, or literal accompaniment.

ex: その一言{ひとこと}をめぐって、ずっと喧嘩{けんか}してた。
exEn: We fought endlessly over that one remark.
note: A contested point. Usually conflict.

ex: 友達{ともだち}を通{つう}じて、あとから聞{き}いた。
exEn: I heard about it later through a friend.
note: Medium, intermediary, or a whole span of time.

ex: みなみをはじめ、みんな心配{しんぱい}してくれた。
exEn: Minami and everyone else worried about me.
note: Names the leading example of a group.

ex: 実話{じつわ}をもとにした映画{えいが}なんだって。
exEn: Apparently it's a film based on a true story.
note: Source material.

ex: データに基{もと}づいて決{き}めたい。
exEn: I want to decide based on the data.
note: Formal basis — rules, evidence, principles.

ex: この業界{ぎょうかい}においては、よくあることらしい。
exEn: In this industry it's apparently common.
note: Formal setting marker. Written Japanese.

ex: あの人{ひと}のもとで、三年{さんねん}働{はたら}いた。
exEn: I worked under him for three years.
note: Under someone's supervision or influence.

ex: 二年{にねん}にわたって、ずっとそうだった。
exEn: For two whole years, that's how it was.
note: A span of time or space, emphasised as long.

ex: 発表{はっぴょう}に先立{さきだ}って、資料{しりょう}を配{くば}った。
exEn: Prior to the presentation, we handed out materials.
note: Formal 'before'. Business Japanese.

ex: 入社{にゅうしゃ}に際{さい}して、挨拶{あいさつ}をさせられた。
exEn: On joining the company, I was made to give a greeting.
note: Formal ceremony-adjacent 'when'.

ex: 部長{ぶちょう}に代{か}わって、わたしが説明{せつめい}した。
exEn: In place of the manager, I gave the explanation.
note: Substitution for a person or thing.

ex: 手伝{てつだ}う代{か}わりに、ごはんおごってよ。
exEn: I'll help, but you're buying me dinner in return.
note: Exchange or substitution. Very common in speech.

ex: 期待{きたい}に応{こた}えたくて、無理{むり}しすぎた。
exEn: I pushed myself too hard trying to live up to expectations.
note: Meeting a request, hope, or expectation.

ex: 初心者{しょしんしゃ}向{む}けの本{ほん}から始{はじ}めたら？
exEn: Why not start with a book aimed at beginners?
note: Deliberately targeted at that audience.

ex: この部屋{へや}、南向{みなみむ}きだから明{あか}るいんだ。
exEn: This room faces south, so it's bright.
note: Suitability or physical orientation.

ex: 工事中{こうじちゅう}につき、こっちの道{みち}は通{とお}れない。
exEn: Due to construction, you can't use this road.
note: Signboard Japanese. Also 'per unit'.

ex: もし日本{にほん}に住{す}むとしたら、どこがいい？
exEn: If you were to live in Japan, where would you pick?
note: Hypothetical premise.

ex: やってみないことには、分{わ}からないよ。
exEn: You won't know unless you try.
note: Without X, Y can't happen. Always negative.

ex: 毎日{まいにち}少{すこ}しやりさえすれば、伸{の}びるよ。
exEn: If you just do a little every day, you'll improve.
note: One sufficient action.

ex: 行{い}くかどうかは、天気{てんき}次第{しだい}。
exEn: Whether we go depends on the weather.
note: Outcome hinges on that factor.

ex: 雨{あめ}も降{ふ}れば、風{かぜ}も強{つよ}い。
exEn: It's raining and the wind is strong too.
note: Lists two parallel facts, same polarity.

ex: 仕事{しごと}やら締{し}め切{き}りやらで、ばたばたしてる。
exEn: What with work and deadlines, everything's hectic.
note: A jumble of things, usually overwhelming.

ex: わたしなんて、まだまだだよ。
exEn: Someone like me? I've got a long way to go.
note: Belittles the thing before it — sometimes yourself.

ex: あれ、名前{なまえ}なんだったっけ。
exEn: Wait, what was the name again?
note: Fishing for something you half-remember. Casual only.

ex: もう少{すこ}しで乗{の}り過{す}ごすところだった。
exEn: I very nearly missed my stop.
note: A near miss that didn't happen.

ex: 電気{でんき}つけっぱなしで寝{ね}ちゃった。
exEn: I fell asleep with the lights left on.
note: A state left uncorrected, usually carelessly.

ex: 読{よ}みかけの本{ほん}が三冊{さんさつ}ある。
exEn: I've got three half-read books lying around.
note: Started and not finished.

ex: 一日{いちにち}で読{よ}み切{き}っちゃった。
exEn: I finished the whole thing in a day.
note: Carry through to the very end.

ex: 多{おお}すぎて、食{た}べ切{き}れない。
exEn: It's too much — I can't finish it.
note: Exceeds your capacity.

ex: つらくても、最後{さいご}までやり抜{ぬ}きたい。
exEn: Even if it's hard, I want to see it through.
note: Persevere to the end despite difficulty.

ex: 前置{まえお}き抜{ぬ}きで言{い}うね。
exEn: I'll say it without any preamble.
note: Omitting something normally included.

ex: うちは金曜{きんよう}、早{はや}く帰{かえ}っていいことになってる。
exEn: At my place the rule is we can leave early on Fridays.
note: An established rule or arrangement.

ex: 最近{さいきん}、寝{ね}てばかりいる。
exEn: Lately I do nothing but sleep.
note: Repetitive to a fault. Mildly critical.

ex: 言{い}われたとおりにやったのに、直{なお}された。
exEn: I did it exactly as told and it still got changed.
note: Matching an instruction or expectation.

ex: つまり、もう終{お}わったということだね。
exEn: So what you mean is, it's over.
note: Either reported speech or a restatement.

ex: おいしいことはおいしいけど、高{たか}い。
exEn: It's tasty enough, but it's expensive.
note: Concedes the point before objecting.

ex: 何度{なんど}聞{き}いても、答{こた}えようとしなかった。
exEn: However often I asked, he wouldn't answer.
note: Someone's persistent unwillingness.

ex: たまには、ぱっと使{つか}おうではないか。
exEn: Let's splash out for once, shall we.
note: Rousing suggestion. She uses it as a joke.

ex: 忘{わす}れないように、メモしとく。
exEn: I'll write it down so I don't forget.
note: Purpose with a non-volitional verb.

ex: 心{こころ}を込{こ}めて作{つく}ったんだよ。
exEn: I made it with real care.
note: Feeling deliberately poured into an action.

ex: あなたあっての毎日{まいにち}、なんてね。
exEn: My days only work because of you — kidding, kidding.
note: X couldn't exist without Y. Quite emotional.

ex: 雨{あめ}だけど、寒{さむ}くないだけましか。
exEn: It's raining, but at least it isn't cold.
note: Finding the small mercy in a bad situation.

ex: 一度{いちど}も振{ふ}り返{かえ}ることなく、行{い}っちゃった。
exEn: He left without looking back even once.
note: Formal 〜ないで. Often final-sounding.

ex: あれはもう、別{わか}れたも同然{どうぜん}だった。
exEn: At that point we'd as good as broken up.
note: Practically equivalent, if not formally so.

ex: {name}ったら、また無理{むり}してる。
exEn: Honestly, you're overdoing it again.
note: Affectionate exasperation at someone.

ex: なんか、忙{いそが}しいとか言{い}ってたよ。
exEn: He said something about being busy, apparently.
note: Vague quotation. Softens and distances.

ex: 子{こ}どもだって、それくらい分{わ}かるよ。
exEn: Even a child would understand that much.
note: Either 'even' or casual hearsay, from context.

ex: それ、けっこう上手{じょうず}なんじゃない？
exEn: That's pretty good, I'd say?
note: Soft opinion dressed as a question. Extremely common.

ex: 放課後{ほうかご}、屋上{おくじょう}でよくだべったものだ。
exEn: We used to sit around talking on the roof after school.
note: Fond recollection of a repeated past habit. The nostalgia is the whole point — plain 〜た is neutral.

ex: 卒業{そつぎょう}してから、あの子{こ}とは会{あ}ってないきり。
exEn: I haven't seen her once since we graduated.
note: Something happened once and the expected follow-up never came.

ex: 高校{こうこう}というと、まず自転車{じてんしゃ}を思{おも}い出{だ}す。
exEn: When I think high school, the first thing is the bicycle.
note: Picks a topic up and runs with the first association.

ex: 忘{わす}れたにしても、あの言{い}い方{かた}はないと思{おも}う。
exEn: Even if he forgot, that was no way to say it.
note: Concedes the excuse and objects anyway. Useful when she's being fair to someone who wasn't.

ex: 楽{たの}しい思{おも}い出{で}があるからといって、戻{もど}りたいわけじゃない。
exEn: Just because there are happy memories doesn't mean I want to go back.
note: Blocks an inference someone might draw. Almost always paired with a negative.

ex: 思{おも}い出{だ}せば思{おも}い出{だ}すほど、細{こま}かいことまで蘇{よみがえ}る。
exEn: The more I remember, the more the small details come back.
note: Already in the set as 〜ば〜ほど; this variant is tagged to the memory threads.

en: after all that, in the end
ex: 散々{さんざん}悩{なや}んだあげく、結局{けっきょく}買{か}わなかった。
exEn: After agonising endlessly, in the end I didn't buy it.
note: A long, usually tiring process ending badly. Always past tense.

ex: 台風{たいふう}で電車{でんしゃ}が止{と}まるおそれがある。
exEn: There's a risk the trains stop because of the typhoon.
note: Formal warning of a bad possibility. Common in news and notices.

ex: あの説明{せつめい}は、正直{しょうじき}理解{りかい}しがたい。
exEn: That explanation is honestly hard to accept.
note: Not physically difficult — psychologically resistant. 信じがたい is the common one.

ex: わたしは考{かんが}えすぎるきらいがある。
exEn: I have a tendency to overthink.
note: A criticised habitual tendency. Formal, and never about good traits.

en: living up to it, no wonder
ex: 毎日{まいにち}練習{れんしゅう}してるだけのことはある。
exEn: No wonder — you practise every day.
note: Praise: the result justifies the effort. Warmer than 〜だけあって.

ex: 焦{あせ}っても仕方{しかた}ないよ。人生{じんせい}ってそういうものだ。
exEn: No use rushing. That's just what life is.
note: States a general truth with a touch of resignation or admonishment.

ex: 高{たか}ければいいというものではない。
exEn: It isn't necessarily the case that expensive is better.
note: Rejects an over-simple rule. Pairs with ば or たら.

ex: この写真{しゃしん}を見{み}ると、笑{わら}わないではいられない。
exEn: Looking at this photo I can't help laughing.
note: Same force as 〜ずにはいられない, slightly more colloquial.

ex: この字{じ}は兄{あに}のに相違{そうい}ない。
exEn: This handwriting is without doubt my brother's.
note: Formal, written 〜に違いない. Rare in speech — she uses it half-jokingly.

ex: あの人{ひと}が怒{おこ}ったのは、想像{そうぞう}に難{かた}くない。
exEn: It isn't hard to imagine he was angry.
note: Almost always 想像に難くない. Written register.

ex: この曲{きょく}には、胸{むね}に来{く}るものがある。
exEn: There's something about this song that gets to you.
note: Names a quality you feel but can't fully specify.

ex: この天気{てんき}じゃ中止{ちゅうし}もやむを得{え}ない。
exEn: In this weather, cancelling is unavoidable.
note: Formal acceptance of a bad but necessary outcome.

ex: 引{ひ}っ越{こ}しをきっかけに、写真{しゃしん}を撮{と}り始{はじ}めた。
exEn: Moving house is what got me into photography.
note: The specific event that started something. Neutral in tone.

en: on the occasion of, prompted by
ex: 転職{てんしょく}を契機{けいき}に、生活{せいかつ}が変{か}わった。
exEn: Changing jobs was the turning point for my routine.
note: Formal 〜をきっかけに. Business and written Japanese.

ex: 経験{けいけん}を問{と}わず応募{おうぼ}できるらしい。
exEn: Apparently you can apply regardless of experience.
note: Formal 'irrespective of'. Common in notices and job ads.

ex: 味{あじ}はともかく、見{み}た目{め}がひどい。
exEn: Taste aside, it looks terrible.
note: Parks one issue to get to the one that matters.

ex: 冗談{じょうだん}はさておき、本題{ほんだい}に入{はい}ろう。
exEn: Joking aside, let's get to the point.
note: Sets a whole subject down. 冗談はさておき is the set phrase.

ex: 努力{どりょく}することなしに、上達{じょうたつ}はしない。
exEn: Without making an effort, you don't improve.
note: Formal 〜ないで. Usually followed by a negative.

ex: 睡眠{すいみん}を削{けず}ってまで、やることじゃない。
exEn: It's not worth going so far as to cut your sleep.
note: Marks an extreme the speaker finds excessive.

ex: 三年{さんねん}ぶりに実家{じっか}に帰{かえ}った。
exEn: I went home for the first time in three years.
note: Time elapsed since the last occurrence. Very common in speech.

ex: 三{さん}ヶ月{かげつ}悩{なや}んだ末{すえ}に、やっと買{か}った。
exEn: After three months of agonising, I finally bought it.
note: A long deliberate process reaching a decision. 〜あげく is its negative twin.

ex: 引{ひ}き受{う}けた上{うえ}は、きちんとやる。
exEn: Now that I've taken it on, I'll do it properly.
note: Resolve following from a commitment. Close to 〜以上は, slightly stiffer.

ex: 一人{ひとり}で過{す}ごす正月{しょうがつ}は、寂{さび}しい限{かぎ}りだ。
exEn: A New Year spent alone is as lonely as it gets.
note: Intensifies an emotion adjective. Slightly literary.

ex: 結局{けっきょく}、言{い}えずじまいだった。
exEn: In the end I never managed to say it.
note: Regret that an intention was never carried out.

ex: この量{りょう}じゃ、今日{きょう}は終{お}わりそうにない。
exEn: At this volume it doesn't look like finishing today.
note: Negative of 〜そうだ — appearances say no.

ex: 今{いま}から急{いそ}いだところで、間{ま}に合{あ}わない。
exEn: Even if I hurry now, I won't make it.
note: A pointless hypothetical. Always followed by a negative outcome.

ex: 軽{かる}い気持{きも}ちのつもりで始{はじ}めたのに、本気{ほんき}になってる。
exEn: I started meaning it lightly and now I'm serious.
note: You believed X, though reality differed. Also 'with the intention of'.

ex: 今年{ことし}こそ、弾{ひ}けるようになってみせる。
exEn: This year I'll show you I can play it.
note: Determination with an audience in mind. Stronger than 〜する.

ex: 春{はる}とはいえ、まだ風{かぜ}が冷{つめ}たい。
exEn: Spring though it may be, the wind is still cold.
note: Concedes a label then contradicts it. Written-leaning but used in speech.

ex: 新{あたら}しい担当{たんとう}を受{う}けるに当{あ}たって、少{すこ}し不安{ふあん}もある。
exEn: On taking the new accounts, I do have some anxiety.
note: Formal 'when doing (something significant)'. Business register.

ex: 行{い}くにせよ行{い}かないにせよ、早{はや}めに決{き}めたい。
exEn: Whether I go or not, I want to decide soon.
note: Formal 〜にしても. Often doubled for either/or.

ex: 影響{えいきょう}は仕事{しごと}にとどまらず、生活{せいかつ}全体{ぜんたい}に及{およ}んでる。
exEn: The effect isn't limited to work; it reaches my whole life.
note: Formal escalation — reaches beyond the obvious scope.

ex: 間{ま}に合{あ}わせるべく、朝{あさ}から動{うご}いてる。
exEn: I've been at it since morning in order to make the deadline.
note: Formal 〜ために. Written Japanese; she uses it wryly.

ex: ここで諦{あきら}めるようでは、続{つづ}かないよね。
exEn: If I give up here, it won't last.
note: A negative condition leading to a bad conclusion. Mildly critical.

ex: 人目{ひとめ}も構{かま}わず、駅{えき}で泣{な}いてる人{ひと}がいた。
exEn: Someone was crying at the station, heedless of onlookers.
note: Ignoring something one normally would mind.

ex: 電気{でんき}をつけたまま寝{ね}てしまった。
exEn: I fell asleep with the light still on.
note: A state left unchanged while something else happens.

ex: 残{のこ}るはあと一日{いちにち}のみ。
exEn: Only one day remains.
note: Formal だけ. Notices, signage, and deliberate emphasis.

ex: 疲{つか}れた日{ひ}は、早{はや}く寝{ね}るに限{かぎ}る。
exEn: On a tiring day, nothing beats an early night.
note: The speaker's confident recommendation.

ex: 急{いそ}いでる日{ひ}に限{かぎ}って、電車{でんしゃ}が遅{おく}れる。
exEn: It's precisely on the days I'm rushing that the train is late.
note: Bad luck landing on the worst possible occasion.
